headline: Sunrise Bakery Celebrates 847th Customer With Free Croissant, Emotional Speech
summary: Local bakery owner Marge Hollister presented complimentary pastry and 12-minute tribute to bewildered Tuesday morning patron.
content:
What began as a simple request for a blueberry muffin turned into an unexpected ceremony Tuesday morning when Sunrise Bakery owner Marge Hollister announced that regular customer Dennis Pruitt was officially the shop's 847th unique customer.

"I've been tracking this since we opened," Hollister explained, gesturing to a hand-drawn chart behind the register that appears to document every customer who has ever entered the establishment. "Eight-four-seven is a very significant number in baking. It's the optimal temperature for proving dough, if you use a very specific and probably incorrect thermometer."

Pruitt, 34, who simply wanted breakfast before his shift at the hardware store, stood frozen with his complimentary croissant as Hollister delivered what witnesses described as "somewhere between a toast and a TED talk" about the journey of small business ownership.

"She mentioned her grandmother, the wheat harvest of 2019, and something about croissants being 'edible architecture,'" said fellow customer Amy Chen, who had been waiting in line for approximately eight minutes. "It was beautiful, in a way that made me late for work."

The bakery has been open for three years. When asked why it took this long to reach 847 customers, Hollister noted that she has "very strict criteria" for what constitutes a unique customer, declining to elaborate further.

Pruitt has reportedly not returned since the ceremony.
author: Janet Reeves, Community Correspondent
